shortName: University of California, San Francisco, School of Medicine

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The School of Medicine welcomes applicants from all ethnic, economic, and cultural backgrounds without discrimination.  The curriculum includes both coursework and practical opportunities focused on narrowing health care disparities. For more information, visit https://meded.ucsf.edu/student-services/diversity-equity-and-inclusion-programs
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Many students request an extension of their medical education for an extra year to do research or other scholarly work, to obtain an additional degree, or to have some additional time for maternity/paternity leave. In general, the School of Medicine is supportive of students extending their program for a year, and approximately one-third of UCSF students do so. The purpose of this policy is to provide guidelines for such extensions and to describe the process for requesting an extended program, which must be approved by the Associate Dean of Curriculum. For more information, visit http://meded.ucsf.edu/ume/extending .
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Please see our website on Student Life at https://meded.ucsf.edu/md-program/current-students/student-services/student-organizations
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The main UCSF campus is located in the center of San Francisco, a short walk from Golden Gate Park and no more than 10 minutes from the Pacific Ocean.  Downtown San Francisco, easily accessible by car or public transportation, is located approximately two miles from the main campus.  Other major UCSF teaching sites include Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital, the VA Medical Center, the Cancer Center, and the new Mission Bay campus. The surrounding area of northern California provides a natural backdrop and opportunities for recreation that are hard to match.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: For detailed information about housing, please visit the UCSF Housing Services Web site at https://campuslifeserviceshome.ucsf.edu/housing
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
UCSF strives to provide support for our students' mental and physical health, as well as spiritual, financial, environmental, and social well-being. Our priority is to support our students well-being through a variety of resources and programs available on-campus and through the medical school, including: dedicated staff and faculty advisors, Medical Student Well-Being Program (MSWB), Therapy Services Affiliated with UCSF , UCSF Student Health and Counseling Services, Wellness and Mental Health Committee, MedPeers Program, and Online Mindfulness Resources.  

More information on each of these areas can be found here: https://meded.ucsf.edu/current-students/student-services/medical-student-well-being
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: UCSF operates a shuttle system that connects the San Francisco locations (Parnassus, Mission Bay, Mount Zion, ZSFG, and the VAMC). The shuttles are free for students and many students take advantage of the UCSF shuttles. During Foundations 2, many students find it more convenient to own a car, as they may have rotations that take them to UCSF sites outside of San Francisco. Learn more at https://meded.ucsf.edu/md-program/current-students/student-services/clinical-learning-sites.

medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students begin patient interaction as early as the first year.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Integrated, active learning model including lectures, small groups, early clinical exposure, research, and team-based, inquiry-driven instruction.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clerkship education and workplace learning begins on the first day with the Clinical Microsystems Clerkship and continues through Foundations 2.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: UCSF does not have a prematriculation program.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The Bridges curriculum at UCSF (meded.ucsf.edu/bridges-curriculum) will enable students to work within complex systems to improve healthcare and advance science for future generations of patients. The Bridges Curriculum is a three-phase, fully integrated curriculum delivered over four years. Bridges will include early longitudinal immersion in clinical teams and an inquiry-focused curriculum. The curriculum is divided into three phases-Foundations I, Foundations II, and Career Launch-with three curricular elements woven throughout. The three curricular elements of foundational sciences, clinical and systems applications, and inquiry activities will serve to further deepen and enrich the educational experience of our students. Bridges will provide dedicated time for scholarly projects, individualized mentorship and advising, and opportunities to individualize education for career goals. For more information, visit https://meded.ucsf.edu/md-program/current-students/curriculum/bridges-curriculum-overview
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: UCSF School of Medicine offers students longitudinal, mentored research through its Inquiry Curriculum with protected time and diverse project options. This is supported by a highly research-intensive environment—UCSF consistently ranks among the top NIH-funded institutions (#1 in 9 of the past 10 years), with strengths across nearly all departments. The school is known for pioneering biomedical discovery and translating findings into clinical and population health impact. Its collaborative culture emphasizes data sharing, cross-disciplinary partnerships, and innovation across basic, clinical, and translational research. Students benefit from broad opportunities to engage in meaningful research aimed at improving care, advancing technology, and promoting health equity.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: The core teaching hospitals are Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital, San Francisco VA Medical Center, UCSF Medical Center, the UCSF Medical Center at Mission Bay and UCSF Fresno.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The UCSF School of Medicine is dedicated to excellence in education, research, and patient care. Woven throughout all of these pursuits is a strong commitment to public service. The UCSF School of Medicine earns its greatest distinction from the quality of its students and its outstanding faculty -- including seven Nobel laureates, 61 National Academy of Sciences members, 75 American Academy of Arts and Sciences members, 112 National Academy of Medicine members, and 17 Howard Hughes Medical Institute investigators. For more information, visit https://www.ucsf.edu/about/achievements#honors.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
UC San Francisco (UCSF) is the leading university dedicated to advancing health worldwide through preeminent biomedical research, graduate-level education in the life sciences and health professions, and excellence in patient care.

Within our overarching advancing health worldwide mission, UCSF is devoted at every level to serving the public.

UCSF’s commitment to public service dates to the founding of its predecessor institution, Toland Medical College, in 1864. Born out of the overcrowded and unsanitary conditions of Gold Rush-era San Francisco, Toland Medical College trained doctors to elevate the standards of public health in the burgeoning city.

By 1873, the University of California acquired the college and forged a partnership with San Francisco General Hospital that continues to this day and serves as a model for delivering leading-edge care at a public safety-net hospital.

Today UCSF’s public mission goes beyond San Francisco and delivers a substantial impact on a national and global level by innovating health care approaches for the world’s most vulnerable populations, training the next generation of doctors, nurses, dentists, pharmacists and scientists; supporting elementary and high school education; and translating scientific discoveries into better health for everyone.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout:
The San Joaquin Valley (SJV) PRIME+ program is a multi-campus baccalaureate/MD program designed to expand high-quality medical education in the San Joaquin Valley. Through a partnership between UCSF, UCSF Fresno, and UC Merced, the program supports future physicians serving the San Joaquin Valley.   

The program includes a four-year baccalaureate, leading into the UCSF Doctor of Medicine curriculum. All elements of the program, offered through UC Merced and UCSF Fresno, focus on preparing a physician workforce to address communities' unmet health and health care needs in the San Joaquin Valley.

High school graduates are accepted into the program and complete the eight-year program by earning their baccalaureate degree at UC Merced and Doctor of Medicine through UCSF. The program takes place entirely in the San Joaquin Valley with the goal of increasing graduates entering residency programs in the region that will practice and care for Valley community members.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: When available, committee letters are preferred.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: When a committee letter or letter packet is available, it is our preference to receive committee letters. If individual letters are sent, please prefer at least two letters from instructors.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Consists of two double-blind interviews, each lasting 45 minutes to one hour.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: There are no special requirements related to the school or state for non-resident or international applicants. Applications from US citizens, Permanent Residents and those with DACA considered.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: For detailed information on our admissions policies, process, and other relevant details, please visit https://meded.ucsf.edu/prospective-students/md-program-admissions/md-program-application-process.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Our admissions committee considers the most recent MCAT score when multiple scores are available.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: UCSF does not limit applicants based on GPA from any institution.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: All completed credit hours from accredited institutions, including postbaccalaureate and graduate coursework, will be considered for eligibility.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We accept all coursework completed at a community college, provided it is from an accredited institution. Premedical students should pursue a four-year undergraduate curriculum and obtain a baccalaureate degree before entering medical school. A maximum of 105 quarter units can be transferred from a community college.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants who are invited to interview may submit up to two application updates: one at the time of interview and a second any time post-interview. Letters of interest or intent are accepted from applicants offered a position on the waitlist only.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The technical standards have several broad categories including observation; communication; clinical skills; intellectual-conceptual, integrative, and cognitive skills; social and behavioral skills; and ethical and legal standards.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Scholarships are awarded to entering students primarily on the basis of need. General financial support is awarded through the Student Financial Aid Office. Aid packages consist of a combination of loans, grants-in-aid, and scholarships. Financial aid is only available to U.S. citizens or permanent residents. For detailed information, please visit http://finaid.ucsf.edu

medSchoolPrograms.name: UC Berkeley/UCSF Joint Medical Program
medSchoolPrograms.deadline: Applicants select the Joint Medical Program (JMP) on the secondary application.
Students apply in their third year of medical school

medSchoolPrograms.info: There are four distinctive programs available that require a stated interest at the time of the secondary application. The four programs are the UCB-UCSF Joint Medical Program (JMP), the Medical Scientist Training Program (MSTP), the Program in Medical Education for the Urban Underserved (PRIME-US), and the San Joaquin Valley Program in Medical Education (SJV PRIME). The UCB-UCSF Joint Medical Program is a five-year program leading to a graduate degree from UC Berkeley and an MD degree from UCSF. The MSTP is a combined MD/PhD program that prepares students for careers as physician-scientists. PRIME-US is a five-year program for medical students interested in devoting their careers to serving urban underserved populations and/or conducting research focused on the health of urban underserved communities. SJV PRIME students focus on serving populations in the central valley. More information about all program options can be found at https://meded.ucsf.edu/degrees-and-programs.

The UCSF School of Medicine offers a comprehensive, structured post baccalaureate graduate certificate program designed for individuals who have been unsuccessful in gaining admission to medical school or who have completed the required undergraduate coursework, but feel they need more preparation before initiating the medical school application process. The program is designed for individuals from disadvantaged backgrounds or underserved communities.

The UCSF program is designed to help individuals increase their chances of gaining admission to medical school by offering intensive MCAT review, assistance with medical school application preparation, science courses at UC Berkeley Extension, seminars on health care issues in underserved communities, and academic skills workshops.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicants on the alternate list are not considered until after the April 30 deadline.

medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Coursework must be completed at accredited institutions and our preference is for coursework taken within ten years of matriculation.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: UCSF students must have demonstrated the ability to perform at a very high level in their prior academic pursuits. Among the many applicants who meet this essential criterion, the school seeks to create a student community that is characterized by diversity in background, extra-curricular talents, academic interests, and career aspirations. There is no single mold that defines a UCSF student. UCSF wants some students who aspire to become terrific doctors, some who will become great scientists, some who will be leaders in health policy, and so on. The goal is to create the most stimulating and enjoyable possible environment in which to live and learn. For further details regarding the admissions process, please visit the School of Medicine's web site at http://meded.ucsf.edu/admissions-md-program
